methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 910 NSCLC patients (2014-2021) with clearly defined eligibility, algorithmic line-of-therapy assignment, manual chart verification, and Kaplan-Meier estimation of OS and rwPFS. The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including single-center design, exclusion of trial patients, algorithmic misclassification risk, and absence of multivariable adjustment, which caps causal inference. No propensity matching, no adjustment for confounders, and temporal comparisons are descriptive only.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study describes real-world treatment evolution at an Italian center before and after ICI availability, showing first-line ICI uptake rising from 0% to 58% (2014-2021) and median OS improving from 6.0-7.4 months (2014-2017) to 8.4-15.9 months (2018-2021). Findings reinforce ESMO guideline-consistent practice but do not change guidelines. As a single-center, uncontrolled retrospective case series/low-quality cohort with no adjusted comparisons, it maps to Oxford LoE 4.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational cohort reporting follows STROBE-adjacent structure with explicit eligibility, variables, ethics approval (IRST Area Vasta Romagna #3366), and declared limitations, but there is no STROBE checklist citation or registration. Missing-data handling is only mentioned for dates (middle-of-month imputation) without a full completeness table. No data availability statement is visible in the provided text; the EHR is proprietary (CCE Log80) and no code sharing is mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: The contribution is incremental: it replicates multiple prior Onco-Optimise / I-O Optimise country analyses (Canada, UK, Sweden, Germany, Netherlands, Denmark, Portugal) in a single Italian center that had already published an earlier analysis (Danesi et al. [24]). The authors themselves frame the work as aligning with and extending prior real-world studies rather than generating new mechanistic or methodological insight.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear IMRaD structure, consistent terminology, and appropriate use of Sankey diagrams, Kaplan-Meier plots, and summary tables. Numbers, CIs, and temporal comparisons are reported consistently across abstract, results, and discussion. Minor issues include some redundancy between results and discussion and a truncated reference to the prior Danesi analysis (REDACTED fragment).

key_strengths: Large single-center cohort (n=910) spanning pre- and post-immunotherapy era (2014-2021) with near-complete follow-up through 2022
Temporal granularity showing first-line anti-PD-(L)1 uptake rising from 0% to 58% with parallel OS improvement (6.0-7.4 to 8.4-15.9 months)
Transparent acknowledgement of 11 specific limitations including lack of multivariable adjustment and algorithmic misclassification risk
Clear Kaplan-Meier stratification by first-line regimen, PD-L1 expression, histology, and de novo vs recurrent disease
key_concerns: Purely descriptive analysis with no confounder adjustment, propensity matching, or statistical testing of temporal OS differences
Single-center scope limits generalizability beyond the IRST/Emilia-Romagna region
High degree of overlap with prior I-O Optimise analyses and the authors' own Danesi 2022 paper at the same institution (incremental novelty)
No data or code availability statement; proprietary EHR precludes reproducibility
PD-L1 testing was only 9% conclusive in 2016 rising to 89% by 2018, biasing early-era subgroup estimates
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, transparently reported real-world descriptive study that confirms known treatment-paradigm shifts in advanced NSCLC but offers limited novelty and no adjusted inference; suitable for a mid-tier oncology journal with minor revisions.
